program_title: Peer Influence, Social Accountability & Risk Management

metadata.core_objective: Build proactive safety protocols and peer-pressure exit strategies while holding firm accountability for high-risk behaviors.
metadata.key_deliverable: Family Safety Code & Risk Management Protocol

topics.title: Adolescent Social Brain & Peer Gravitation
topics.summary: Understanding neurobiological peer susceptibility and building exit strategies.
key_principles: Limbic sensitivity heightens risk-taking in peer environments.
Low-social-cost scripts lower barriers to exiting unsafe situations.

topics.title: The No-Questions-Asked Safety Code
topics.summary: Establishing an unconditional safety net for emergency transportation and physical protection.
protocol_steps: Establish a secret code word or emoji.
Immediate parent pickup with script deflection.

activities.title: Designing Social Exit Scripts
activities.instructions: Co-create subtle, socially acceptable excuse scripts for high-pressure peer scenarios.

tasks.title: Safety Code Agreement Setup
tasks.action: Finalize code word, emergency response steps, and the 24-hour debrief rule with youth.

quiz.question: Why is equipping teenagers with 'low-social-cost' exit scripts more effective than simply telling them to 'just say no'?
options: A) Teenagers do not know how to speak clearly.
B) Adolescent brains prioritize peer acceptance; exit scripts allow them to escape unsafe situations without risking social rejection.
C) It saves time for parents.
D) Exit scripts guarantee that teenagers will never make mistakes.

quiz.question: What is the primary purpose of a 'No-Questions-Asked' Safety Code?
options: A) To allow teenagers to break every family rule without facing any consequences ever.
B) To prioritize physical safety during an emergency by ensuring the youth gets home safely before any disciplinary debrief occurs.
C) To spy on what the teenager's friends are doing.
D) To eliminate the need for curfews.
